The study was conducted in two phases: a preliminary design analysis and a final design analysis.
Eight air-cooled turbine blade designs in 0.75-in. (0.01905 m), 1.0-in. (0.0254 m), and 1.5-in. (0.0381 m) chord sizes were investigated in the preliminary design phase.
A pin fin convection-cooled configuration and a film-impingement cooled configuration were selected for the final design analysis.
The final designs were analyzed at three turbine inlet total pressures and three cooling air inlet temperatures for each chord size.
The cooling air flow required with a constant turbine inlet total temperature and pressure was determined at three cooling air inlet temperatures for each chord size.
The film-convection cooled designs allowed turbine inlet temperatures about 200°F (111°K) higher than the convection-cooled designs.
The transpiration-cooled design offered an advantage only for the 1.5-in. (0.0381 m) chord size.
A decrease in cooling air inlet temperature produced an increase in turbine inlet temperature capability or a reduction in cooling air flow required.
The turbine inlet pressure range studied had relatively little effect on turbine inlet temperature capability.
An increase in chord size produced a reduction in cooling air flow required for the convection-cooled blade, but this trend was not apparent in the film-convection cooled design.
An estimated life of 1000 hours was obtained for each final design based on a detailed creep relaxation analysis or a maximum metal temperature limit.
Additional studies were conducted on the effects of reducing cooling air inlet pressure and varying flow control orifice sizes for selected conditions.
The study considered the effects of cooling air discharge at the blade tip on turbine tip clearance losses and the efficiency loss due to transpiration cooling of the blades.
The study used a three-dimensional blade surface velocity calculation program (TR-IG) to determine the turbine airfoil surface critical velocity ratio profile.
The stress analysis was conducted using an elastic, inelastic, and creep analysis computer program (X0850).
